q: Work must be done to separate two bodies having opposite charges since they _____ each other.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. Work must be done to separate two bodies having opposite charges since they attract each other. Repel or ignore is not this quantity.

q: Work must be done to bring closer two bodies having the same kind of charge since they _____ each other.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. Work must be done to bring closer two bodies having the same kind of charge since they repel each other. Do not trade repel for attract or neutralize.

q: The work done in separating or bringing charges is stored up in the charged objects as electric _____ energy.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The work done in separating or bringing charges is stored up in the charged objects as electric potential energy. Do not trade potential for kinetic or thermal.

q: The electric potential at a point in an electric field is the work done in bringing a unit positive charge against the electric force from _____ to that point.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The electric potential at a point in an electric field is the work done in bringing a unit positive charge against the electric force from infinity to that point. The origin or the earth is not this quantity.

q: Electric potential is actually the amount of work done, so it is a _____ quantity.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. Electric potential is actually the amount of work done, so it is a scalar quantity. Vector or tensor is not this quantity.

q: The practical unit of electric potential is the _____ (V).
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. The practical unit of electric potential is the volt (V). Do not trade volt for joule or newton.

q: If the work done in bringing +1 coulomb from infinity to a point is 1 joule, the electric potential at that point is 1 joule per coulomb or _____.
e: Coulomb's law: F = K q1 q2 / r². Like charges repel; unlike charges attract. If the work done in bringing +1 coulomb from infinity to a point is 1 joule, the electric potential at that point is 1 joule per coulomb or 1 V. 1 w or 1 n is not this quantity.

q: The electric potential at infinity is taken as _____ by convention.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. The electric potential at infinity is taken as zero by convention. Do not trade zero for one or infinity.

q: The electric potential difference between two points in an electric field is the work done in bringing a unit positive charge from one point to another against _____.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The electric potential difference between two points in an electric field is the work done in bringing a unit positive charge from one point to another against electric force. Magnetic force or gravitational force is not this quantity.

q: A positive charge will move from a point of _____ electric potential to a point of lower electric potential.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. A positive charge will move from a point of higher electric potential to a point of lower electric potential. Lower or zero is not this quantity.

q: A negative charge will move from a point of lower electric potential to a point of _____ electric potential.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. A negative charge will move from a point of lower electric potential to a point of higher electric potential. Lower or zero is not this quantity.

q: The electric potential $V$ at a point is directly proportional to the charge $Q$ and inversely proportional to the _____ $r$ from the charge.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. The electric potential V at a point is directly proportional to the charge Q and inversely proportional to the distance r from the charge. Do not trade distance for square or mass.

q: When determining the total electric potential at a point due to several point charges, the individual electric potentials must be added _____.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. When determining the total electric potential at a point due to several point charges, the individual electric potentials must be added algebraically. Vectorially or geometrically is not this quantity.

q: The work done in moving a charge in an electric field is independent of the _____ taken by the charge.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The work done in moving a charge in an electric field is independent of the path taken by the charge. Do not trade path for speed or time.

q: The work done only depends on the electric potential _____ between two points.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. The work done only depends on the electric potential difference between two points. Do not trade difference for sum or product.

q: The electric potential is the electric potential energy per unit _____ charge.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. The electric potential is the electric potential energy per unit positive charge. Negative or neutral is not this quantity.
